newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end modestly higher in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end modestly higher in heavy trade.

* Toronto stocks ended modestly higher on Monday, as investors paused from last week's record-setting rally * Market awaiting economic data * 92.6 million shares traded worth C$1.3 billion
Toronto stocks edged higher on Monday as investors took a breather from last week's record-setting rally and awaited fresh economic data.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose a modest 2.13 points to close at 5872.69 in brisk turnover of 92.6 million shares worth C$1.3 billion.

Advancing stocks slipped past declines 495 to 491 with 269 issues unchanged. "A little bit of a consolidation. This will probably continue for a few days until some additional economic news comes out," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
Statistics Canada is scheduled to release Canada's consumer price index for October early Tuesday morning.
Inflation-nervous investors will be eyeing other Canadian and U.S. economic numbers due out later in the week.
"Essentially what we're looking for are signs that the economy continues to grow, but at a diminishing pace," Katzin said.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-groups finished higher, led by conglomerates, transport, consumer products and energy.
Precious metals led weak sectors with a 118-point drop due to sluggish gold futures.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Nickel miner Sherritt International topped the most-active list, climbing 0.15 to 8.60 on 3.2 million shares.
Trading in Sherritt was brisk as investors speculated about how the firm would spend its recently raised funds, analysts said.
* Corriente Resources Inc jumped 1.45 to 9.65 on 482,000 shares amid market speculation that the mining company will release positive drilling results soon.
* Saskatchewan Wheat Pool class B soared 1.35 to close at 19.45 on 56,000 shares after hitting a 52-week high of 20.95.
